mechanism_narrative: The continued rise in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, alongside the decline in RESIDENTIAL, signals more out-of-home activity and commuting. That mix should lift retail foot traffic over the next four weeks relative to the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days relative to the prior 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continuing to improve for two more weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below its current level while WORKPLACES stays depressed, people shift more time back outside the home, producing a short-lag increase in RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines by at least 2 points week-on-week from the current level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase within 7 days after RESIDENTIAL drops by at least 2 points while WORKPLACES remains at or below its current level.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both stop improving and flatten near their current depressed levels, retail mobility will keep falling because commuter and errand trips are not re-accelerating. The effect should be visible over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each fail to rise for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain flat or weaker for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A broad rebound in PARKS activity together with GROCERy_PHARM improvement marks warmer-weather outing intensity that spills into nearby retail visits. The retail effect should emerge over two weeks, not immediately.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 3 points from its current level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days after PARKS rises by at least 3 points and GROCERY_PHARM also moves upward.

mechanism_narrative: The persistent rise in GROCERY_PHARM reflects more essential stop patterns and bundled errands. That supports a gradual lift in retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains lower over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM continues to rise or stays above its current level.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT crosses above a less-negative threshold from its current depressed level, it indicates a real easing of movement frictions. That threshold crossing should precede higher retail mobility within two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after TRANSIT crosses above -55 from below.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, when paired with lower RESIDENTIAL time, creates a commuting-plus-errand pattern that compounds retail exposure. This interaction should push RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over 28 days when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve and RESIDENTIAL falls relative to the current snapshot.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, continued weakness in PARKS combined with still-elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates indoor substitution rather than leisure outings. That substitution should keep retail mobility below its recent average over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite PARKS remaining very low and RESIDENTIAL staying above its current level.
